newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New acquisitions boost UAC Nigeria stock.
newsitem.headline: New acquisitions boost UAC Nigeria stock.

text.p: Shares of Nigeria's conglomerate UAC rose at the Nigerian bourse on Wednesday following its announcement of new acquisitions, traders said.
The company, a former Unilever partner, said it recently acquired a 60 percent stake in a multi-purpose mill worth 263 million naira and 47 percent stake in a company producing mineral water.
The monetary value of the second acquisition was not stated, but UAC shares rose 15 kobo to 7.85 naira in reaction to the two deals, traders said.
"Investors think it is a good time to buy the shares, but the news of the acquisition definitely added to the push," said trader Dumebi Ohanwusi of Networth Securities.
"Both companies have synergy with our existing food, packaging and distribution businesses," Bassey Ndiokho, chairman of UAC, told traders on Tuesday.
According to Ndiokho, Grand Cereals and Oil Mills Ltd. (GCOML) "is a multi-purpose mill with three divisions - oil mill, cereal mill and feed mill."
The other acquisition is in Spring Waters Nigeria Ltd. (SWAN), producer of a popular brand of mineral water in the country.
Both companies are located in north central state of Plateau.
UAC, one of the largest and most diversified in Nigeria, is a major player in foods, property, packaging and distribution businesses.
Its turnover reached 9.4 billion naira in 1995 from 3.1 billion in 1995, Ndiokho said.

It became a wholly owned Nigerian company in 1994 when Unilever divested from it. Both have equity interests in Tractor & Equipment Nigeria Ltd., involved in the sale and technical support service for Caterpillar products.
